title: Guidewire Delivers the Open, Secure, and Complete Core Platform for Agentic Insurance
summary: Insurers gain speed and precision across the insurance lifecycle to launch products faster, assess and price risk more effectively, and resolve claims sooner

- Guidewire Delivers the Open, Secure, and Complete Core Platform for Agentic Insurance


Guidewire (NYSE: GWRE) today launched a new platform approach to agentic insurance, giving insurers an open, secure, and complete foundation for putting AI to work across the insurance lifecycle. By bringing together the applications, data, workflows, and controls insurers need, Guidewire sets out a practical model for moving from isolated AI experiments to governed agents that improve the speed and precision of insurance decisions and actions.


“Insurance is a business of decisions and actions made in context,” said Mike Rosenbaum, chief executive officer, Guidewire. “By embedding agentic capabilities where insurers already run their core operations, Guidewire gives agents the context and controls they need to work with speed and precision on a proven durable foundation.”


Guidewire agents run on the same trusted platform as its core applications and work with an insurer’s current data and workflows. For agents to work effectively, they need to know what is true, what has already been done, and what they are allowed to do. The platform’s controls enforce those boundaries with consistent security and a clear audit trail that remains current and secure through ongoing updates.


“We took a platform approach to AI, so agents run on the same platform as the core, with access to an insurer’s context, data, and workflows,” said Diego Devalle, chief product development officer, Guidewire. “The scalability and observability that already support the core now support agents too. That is why insurers can put them to work on live claims and policies, and why developers can build on the same open foundation.”


The examples below represent a sample of Guidewire’s growing portfolio of agents and agentic capabilities across the insurance lifecycle. Guidewire will continue to expand this portfolio, giving insurers more ways to put agents to work within the workflows and controls of the Guidewire platform.


### Agentic underwriting


The speed of competition in the market is putting pressure on insurers to increase product and pricing agility. Guidewire shortens the path from product concept to market, giving underwriters clearer risk context and decision support within the work they already do.


- **Advanced Product Designer** . Product managers can now move products from intent to market-ready in days, with impact analysis, gap detection, and explainable recommendations. Agentic tooling speeds up the work of designing and refining products*.
- **PricingCenter** . Actuaries can move sophisticated pricing models to live rates in days by validating rules, factors, and adjustments while maintaining the established efficiency of promotion to production. This keeps portfolio impact visible. Native integration with PolicyCenter connects pricing decisions directly to policy workflows.*
- **Risk Accumulation App*** . Underwriters and portfolio managers can see concentration and exposure by peril on a map, from a single submission to the whole book. They can check how one risk changes portfolio exposure without leaving their normal workflow.
- **UnderwritingCenter*** . Underwriters gain greater productivity and precision and can quote directly in UnderwritingCenter. It turns raw submissions into clear risk profiles and matches risks to portfolio strategy and appetite. Direct integration moves the quote into PolicyCenter, removing the risk of handoffs.
- **ProNavigator** . Underwriters use embedded AI and Guidewire-developed agents* for submission summaries, relevant risk insights, and next-best actions.


### Agentic claims


Claims teams face similar pressure to act quickly while increasing the precision of each decision. Guidewire puts agentic capabilities in the flow of work, from first notice of loss through adjudication and the broader indemnity supply chain.


- **Concierge** . Claimants connect with autonomous agents by voice or chat. The agents capture full loss details and deliver decision-ready claims to ClaimCenter.
- **ProNavigator** . Adjusters move from context to decision faster with answers, suggestions, and next-best actions from an embedded AI assistant and Guidewire-developed agents.
- **Workers’ Compensation Solution** . Claims teams can help injured workers recover sooner with a connected solution that links claims work with digital tools and AI.


“A claim goes faster when adjusters have the facts from the start,” said Amy Mollin, vice president, product management, Guidewire. “We built agents into ClaimCenter, where the work already happens, to capture the loss, summarize the file, and flag risk. That gives adjusters time back for the decisions and conversations that matter most to claimants and injured parties.”


“Insurers are moving beyond AI experimentation and looking for ways to put agentic AI to work across the insurance lifecycle,” said Karlyn Carnahan, executive partner, Celent. “The next challenge is making these capabilities work within the systems and workflows that run the business. That is where the platform matters. By connecting agents to core data and processes, Guidewire gives insurers a practical path to deploy them in production with the controls they need.”


### Agentic platform and data


Guidewire gives technical teams the infrastructure and current insurance data to put agents into production and govern how they operate.


- **Agentic Framework** . Insurers can use Guidewire-developed agents or build their own, select the model for each task, enforce guardrails, evaluate behavior, and monitor costs.
- **Developer Assistants** . Guidewire-aware assistants help technical teams update code, workflows, and rules faster.
- **DevSpace*** . Developers start sooner in preconfigured cloud environments with built-in Guidewire tooling.
- **Guidewire Data Platform** . Policy, claims, and billing data come together in one place, so agents and predictive models draw on the same data.
- **Data Studio** and **Explore** . Curated P&C datasets are ready to use on day one. Insurers can also draw business insight from their own data.
- **Kaleidoscope*** . Predictive models tuned to an insurer’s own book can also draw on industry and third-party data to fill gaps. Federated learning trains the models where each party’s data resides, so records don't move and privacy is preserved.*


“Innovation is about reimagining how work gets done and giving our people the capabilities to make that possible,” said Tatjana Lalkovic, Chief Technology Officer, Definity. “Guidewire Developer Assistants bring relevant context directly into the development process, helping our teams move from idea to implementation faster while keeping human judgment and our standards at the center. It’s a great example of how we’re using AI to increase the pace of innovation and deliver value to our business, brokers, and customers sooner.”


Guidewire is also using AI to transform how it delivers programs with customers. Across professional services, Guidewire has embedded AI into its implementation methodology, materially reducing migration and implementation timelines. This enables insurers to put new capabilities in the hands of claims and underwriting teams sooner.


Guidewire is demonstrating these advancements this week at[Guidewire Connections](https://connections.guidewire.com/event/d4b3d924-5309-4bf8-9efa-d614c0833aa3/connections-2026) in Las Vegas, where over 3,000 insurers and partners from 36 countries have gathered for the company’s annual customer conference.
